causal_claim.content: Work softening at temperatures higher than 700 °C is attributed to microstructure evolution including dynamic recovery or dynamic recrystallization.

causal_claim.content: The combination of Zener pinning pressure and further retarding pressure from migrated grain boundaries causes delayed recrystallization, which in turn delays strain softening up to 900 °C.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Therefore, while P D is identical, the overall pressure for recrystallization decreases as a result of the Zener pinning pressure ( P Z ) caused by Mn 2 O 3 and further retarding pressure ( P C ) caused by the migrated grain boundary. As RX is delayed due to this, SLM-built equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEA is expected to delay strain softening up to 900 °C.

causal_claim.content: The decrease in overall recrystallization pressure caused by nano-sized oxides and migrated grains results in a lack of extreme flow stress decrease up to ~900 °C.

candidate.rationale: Answering this determines if the current Mn2O3 size (27.3 nm) is optimal for high-temperature strength or if further refinement is required to maximize recrystallization delay.
candidate.decision_use: Guides the selection of powder chemistry or process parameters to tune precipitate size for extreme temperature applications.
answer_requirements: Measure flow stress vs. temperature for samples with varying Mn2O3 precipitate sizes (e.g., 10 nm vs 27.3 nm vs 50 nm) via compression testing.

Perform in-situ TEM or post-mortem microstructural analysis to correlate precipitate size with recrystallization fraction.
evidence_spans: As SLM-built equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEA has a high fraction F v and d of 27.3 nm, P Z increases significantly. Therefore, the overall pressure for RX decreases dramatically.

candidate.question: For SLM-built equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEA in the 700–900 °C regime, does the presence of both dynamic recovery and grain boundary migration (gDRX) co-occurring with dynamic recrystallization (dDRX) explain the sustained flow stress, and can texture control enhance this synergistic effect?
candidate.rationale: Resolves whether the observed high-temperature stability is due to a single mechanism or a complex interplay of multiple recovery/recrystallization modes, which dictates the optimal microstructure design.
candidate.decision_use: Informs whether future studies should focus on manipulating grain boundary mobility (texture control) or dislocation density to further improve high-temperature performance.
answer_requirements: Conduct high-temperature compression tests with varying strain rates to distinguish between dDRX and gDRX contributions via microstructural mapping.
Perform EBSD analysis to quantify the fraction of recrystallized grains versus migrated grain boundaries at different temperatures (700 °C, 800 °C, 900 °C).
Compare the flow stress response of samples with controlled <001> texture vs random texture.

This is a phenomenological characteristic of gDRX, and based on this finding, gDRX is also occur simultaneously in high-temperature deformation of SLM-built HEA with dDRX.
This can be attributed to microstructure evolution (dynamic recovery or dynamic recrystallization) occurring during deformation.

candidate.question: In SLM-built equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEA, does the absence of dendritic segregation and the presence of a dislocation network alone (without elemental segregation) sufficiently explain the superior high-temperature flow stress, or are the nano-sized Mn2O3 particles a mandatory prerequisite?
candidate.rationale: Distinguishes between the contributions of the dislocation network (inherent to SLM) and the oxide particles (specific to composition/process) to the high-temperature mechanism.
candidate.decision_use: Determines if the specific Mn-containing chemistry is necessary for high-temperature performance or if the SLM process alone is sufficient.
answer_requirements: Synthesize SLM-built HEA with a Mn-free composition (e.g., CoCrFeNi) under identical parameters to isolate the dislocation network effect.
Compare the high-temperature (700–900 °C) compression curves and microstructural evolution (recrystallization onset) of Mn-containing vs Mn-free SLM samples.
Measure the Zener pinning pressure (Pz) and recrystallization fraction in both systems.
evidence_spans: In addition, scanning TEM (STEM)-EDS mapping of the cell structure confirmed that elemental segregation did not occur, and this leads to the conclusion that substructures in SLM-built HEA are only formed by dislocation networks (Fig. S2).

The main reason why SLM-built HEA has outstanding mechanical properties is suspected to be due to the dislocation network, fine grain size and nano-sized Mn 2 O 3 that were observed in the initial microstructure.
